sections.overview: Mompha raschkiella is a small European micromoth in the family Momphidae, associated especially with rosebay willowherb.
sections.identification: The adult has a wingspan around 7–11 mm. It can be separated from the similar Mompha locupletella by the latter’s contrasting pale and dark patches near the forewing base.
sections.habitat: It occurs in open, often disturbed places such as heathland, woodland clearings, verges and waste ground.
sections.diet: The caterpillar mines the leaves of rosebay willowherb (Chamerion angustifolium), leaving a blotch-like mine.
sections.behavior: The larva feeds concealed inside a leaf mine; adults are recorded from late spring into summer, with a later flight in some regions.
sections.reproduction: The species has more than one generation in parts of its range; it overwinters as a pupa.
sections.ecology: Its life cycle is tied closely to willowherb leaves. Records on hairy willowherb (Epilobium hirsutum) are considered uncertain by Lepiforum.
sections.conservation: Regional moth atlases describe it as widespread in Britain but locally scarce; these local records do not establish a global population trend.
